newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks end higher, Enersis rallies.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks end higher, Enersis rallies.

text.p: Chilean stocks rebounded to close sharply higher in steady trade on Tuesday with the market bolstered by a recovery in power utility Enersis, which had been hammered in a foreign-led selloff Monday, said dealers.
The rally is expected to resume Wednesday, albeit at a more moderate tempo, said analysts.
"I see the market flattening out a little. The electricals are unlikely to gain more ground as they are already fairly priced," said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
The 40-share index, which shed over two percent Monday, closed up 1.31 percent at 129.0 points.
The broad-market index gained 0.56 percent to 5,635.49 points amid turnover of nine billion pesos.
Traders noted that Enersis rallied on strong fundamentals including hopes of good operating earnings from subsidiary Endesa in the second quarter.
"The selloff yesterday was uncalled for. Fundamentally the company looks fine...the operating side is fine," said Hurd.
Monday's tumble was probably the result of a one-off sale by a mutual fund in New York but traders said fears of further selloffs would hang over the stock for several days.
"Non-one can be 100 percent sure that the seller of Enersis is completely out of the market," said one dealer.
Enersis ended up 2.98 percent at 285.25 pesos, after tumbling six percent Monday.
Other winners included supermarket chains D&S and Santa Isabel which rallied 3.13 percent to 495 pesos and 1.33 percent to 760 pesos respectively.
Losers included bottler Andina, down 0.64 percent at 1,550 pesos and Banco de A.Edwards which shed 0.6 percent at 50 pesos.
